description: Cross-stack password policy contract (QUAL issue 242). Mirrored on both the Go authoritative validator (internal/server/password_policy.go) and the TypeScript SPA pre-flight (src/lib/passwordPolicy.ts). Both sides' tests assert their constants match THIS file. A drift in either constant fails the contract test on the offending side; a drift in this file fails BOTH sides simultaneously, surfacing the missed sync in code review.
adversarialVectorsDescription: Documents the policy's CURRENT behaviour against Unicode adversarial inputs. The validator's character-class checks are deliberately ASCII-only (`isAllAsciiDigits` on the Go side at password_policy.go:138-151, the same on the TS side at passwordPolicy.ts:59-66). The vectors below are NOT bugs the contract demands a fix for; the contract pins the DOCUMENTED behaviour so a future refactor that 'helpfully' normalises inputs to NFKC has to deliberately revisit this contract. If/when the policy is broadened to detect Unicode digit categories, bump `version` and flip the matching `expectViolations` entries.

fullwidthUsername._description: Fullwidth-Latin username (Halfwidth+Fullwidth Forms block, U+FF21..U+FF3A). NFKC would normalise these to ASCII A-Z, after which the containsUsername rule would match. The current ASCII-only check uses raw substring equality (case-insensitive) and does NOT detect this overlap.
fullwidthUsername.policyComment: Intentional: NFKC normalisation is NOT performed. Operator threat model assumes humans typing passwords on standard keyboards; the cross-script confusable surface is out of scope for the password policy. Geode itself accepts the password verbatim; this gap is documented, not silently overlooked.

cjkDigits._description: CJK fullwidth digits (Halfwidth+Fullwidth Forms block, U+FF10..U+FF19). NFKC would normalise these to ASCII 0-9, after which the all-digits weakPattern rule would match. The current ASCII-only check uses 0x30..0x39 and does NOT detect this overlap.
cjkDigits.policyComment: Intentional: see fullwidthUsername. The weak-pattern rule is a best-effort filter, not a load-bearing security gate -- the length floor (12 chars) and the upstream auth boundary do the work.

nbspPassword._description: Password containing only NBSP (U+00A0) and a single visible character. The length check sees 12 code points and passes. The all-same-character check uses raw rune equality so a mix of NBSP + visible chars is NOT detected. A password that is one visible char followed by 11 NBSPs would pass the policy.
nbspPassword.policyComment: Intentional: the policy makes no claim about visual masquerading via whitespace. The threat model is automated dictionary attacks; an attacker who can convince a user to type a password with NBSPs has already won.

nbspAllSame._description: All-NBSP password (12 x U+00A0). The all-same-character check fires (every rune equals U+00A0); the all-digits check does not. WEAKPATTERN is the expected violation.
nbspAllSame.policyComment: Same as `aaaaaaaaaaaa`: the all-same-character rule catches it. NBSP being a non-printing space is incidental -- the rule operates on rune equality.
